weeks.title: My iPad, My Job
weeks.bigIdea: A digital citizen takes care of shared devices and follows the rules. Our iPads cost money, and we share them fairly, just like a good citizen at school.

words.meaning: someone who uses technology in a safe, kind and responsible way
a tool like an iPad, a computer or a phone
doing the right thing, even when no one is watching
something a group pays for and uses together, like our class iPads

activities.title: Learn It: What Is Online?
activities.intro: Let's learn about being online and about our class iPads! Listen carefully, then solve each puzzle to unlock Next.

slides.text: The internet connects computers and iPads all around the world.

do.ask: Which things can connect to the internet? Find all four.

items.label: Teddy bear
items.say: A teddy bear can't go online. Keep looking.

items.label: Paper book
items.say: A paper book can't go online. Keep looking.

items.label: Pencil
items.say: A pencil can't go online. Keep looking.

do.done: You found them all! They can all connect to the internet.

slides.text: When your iPad uses the internet, you are online.

do.ask: Which button turns on the internet? Tap it.

items.label: Battery
items.say: That shows how much battery is left. Try again.

items.label: Wi-Fi
items.say: Yes! Wi-Fi connects the iPad to the internet.

items.label: Volume
items.say: That makes the sound louder. Try again.

items.label: Camera
items.say: That takes pictures. Try again.

do.done: Now this iPad is online!

slides.text: Online, we can learn, watch videos, play games and talk to people far away.

do.ask: Which of these can we do online? Find all four.

items.label: Swim in a pool
items.say: You can't swim online! Keep looking.

items.label: Eat a snack
items.say: You can't eat a snack online! Keep looking.

items.label: Go down a slide
items.say: Slides are at the playground, not online. Keep looking.

do.done: So many things to do online!

slides.text: Being online is like visiting a giant city. Most places are fun and helpful. Some places are not for kids.

do.ask: Read the signs. Which place is not for kids? Tap that door.

items.say: This is the kids library. Fun and helpful! Keep looking.
This is science for kids. Fun and helpful! Keep looking.
This is an art studio. Fun and helpful! Keep looking.
You found it! This place is for grown-ups only. Close the door and tell a grown-up.

do.done: Most places are great. If you find one that is not for kids, tell a grown-up.

slides.text: In a city, we follow safety rules. Online, we follow safety rules too.

do.ask: Tap a light, then tap what it means online.
do.tryAgain: Not that one. Think about what the light means.

b.label: Stop and think before you tap
b.say: Red means stop. Stop and think before you tap.

b.label: Slow down and ask a grown-up
b.say: Yellow means slow down. Ask a grown-up if you're not sure.

b.label: Go! It is safe and OK
b.say: Green means go. It is safe and OK.

do.done: Stop, slow down, go. Those are your online traffic lights!

slides.text: A digital citizen is someone who is safe, kind and responsible online.

do.ask: Is it safe, kind, or responsible? Tap the right badge.

items.label: Keep my password secret
items.say: Keeping a password secret keeps you safe. Try again.

items.label: Say thank you in a message
items.say: Saying thank you is kind. Try again.

items.label: Plug in the iPad when I'm done
items.say: Taking care of the iPad is responsible. Try again.

items.label: Tell a grown-up about a scary video
items.say: Telling a grown-up keeps you safe. Try again.

items.label: Ask a new friend to play
items.say: Including others is kind. Try again.

items.label: Ask before I use an app
items.say: Asking first is responsible. Try again.

do.done: Safe, kind and responsible. That's a digital citizen!

slides.text: iPads cost a lot of money. Our school buys them so everyone in our class can learn.

do.ask: How did our class get these iPads?

items.label: They were free
items.say: iPads are not free. Try again.

items.label: The school bought them with money
items.say: Yes! The school paid money for them.

items.label: They grew on a tree
items.say: Silly! Try again.

do.done: Our iPads were bought with real money.

slides.text: Our class shares iPads. We take care of them so they are ready for the next friend.

do.ask: How do we get the iPad ready for the next friend? Tap the steps in order.
do.done: Thank you! The iPad is ready for the next friend.

slides.text: Sharing is a kind of exchange. We each take a turn, and everyone gets what they need.

do.ask: Our class has 10 iPads and 20 kids. What is a fair way to share?

items.label: Take turns with a timer
items.say: Yes! Taking turns is fair for everyone.

items.label: The fastest kids get them
items.say: Then some kids never get a turn. Try again.

items.label: Keep one in my desk all day
items.say: Then other kids can't use it. Try again.

do.done: Fair sharing is how our class community works.

check.text: Which one can NOT go online?

choices.feedback: Yes! A paper book can't connect to the internet.
An iPad can go online with Wi-Fi. Which one can't?
A smart TV can go online. Which one can't?

activities.title: Meet the iPad
activities.intro: Our school paid a lot of money for this iPad, so let's learn how it works. Listen, then tap the part.

parts.info: The screen is glass. Touch it gently with one clean finger.
parts.clue: Which part do you touch to use the apps?

parts.info: The camera takes pictures. Only take photos when your teacher says it's OK.
The top button turns the screen on and off.
parts.clue: Which part turns the screen on and off?

parts.info: The volume buttons make the sound louder or quieter.
parts.clue: Which part makes the sound louder?

parts.info: The charging port is where the charger goes. Push the plug in gently.
parts.clue: Which part does the charger go into?

activities.clueIntro: Great! Now a harder round. Listen to the clue and tap the part.

activities.title: iPad Care
activities.intro: Our class iPads are shared. Is it a good way to care for them? Sort each card.

cards.why: Two hands keep it from falling.
We walk so we don't drop it. Fixing a broken iPad costs a lot of money.

cards.text: Put your drink right next to it
cards.why: Spills can break an iPad, and repairs cost a lot of money. Keep drinks far away.

cards.text: Put it back in the cart and plug it in
cards.why: Then it is charged and ready for the next friend.

cards.text: Tap the screen with a pencil
cards.why: Pencils can scratch the screen, and a new screen costs money. Use your finger.

cards.text: Tell a teacher if it breaks
cards.why: Telling right away is the responsible thing to do.
This iPad is a shared resource. Leave it the way you found it.

cards.text: Use the apps your teacher picks
cards.why: That keeps us safe and learning.

cards.text: Clean the screen with a wet paper towel
cards.why: Water can get inside. Ask your teacher how to clean it.

cards.text: Hand it to a friend with two hands
cards.why: Two hands for passing, too!

cards.text: Turn the sound all the way up without headphones
cards.why: Loud sound bothers others. Use headphones.

cards.text: Change the settings to make it yours
cards.why: Class iPads are shared. Only the teacher changes settings.

cards.text: Remember the iPad cost our school money
cards.why: Knowing it costs money helps us take good care of it.

activities.title: Walk It to the Cart
activities.intro: Fixing a dropped iPad costs a lot of money. Drag the iPad to the cart. Walk slowly, and go around things on the floor.
activities.tooFast: Whoa! Walk, don't run with your iPad. Back to the start.
activities.roundDone: Safe in the cart! No broken screen to pay for.
activities.nextRound: Here comes another iPad. Walk it to the cart.

hazards.say: Oops! Keep the iPad away from drinks.
Oops! Don't trip on the backpack.
Oops! Watch out for the ball.
Oops! Watch out for blocks on the floor.
Oops! Keep the iPad away from drinks.

movers.say: Oops! The ball rolled into you. Watch where it's going.
Oops! Watch out for the toy car.

activities.title: What Would You Do?
activities.intro: Read each story. What is the responsible thing to do?

items.text: You finish your iPad work early. What do you do?

choices.feedback: Let's check with the teacher first. They may have a job for you.

choices.text: Ask the teacher what to do next
choices.feedback: Yes! Asking is the responsible choice.

choices.text: Watch a video on my own
choices.feedback: Ask first. Your teacher picks what is OK to watch.

items.text: You open the class iPad and see a friend's work from before.

choices.text: Leave it and tell the teacher
choices.feedback: Yes! That work belongs to your friend.
That is your friend's work. Leave it and tell the teacher.

choices.text: Open their work to see it
choices.feedback: That work belongs to your friend. Leave it and tell the teacher.

items.text: A friend says: I'll give you my cookie if you let me have your turn on the class iPad all day.

choices.text: Say: The class iPad isn't mine to trade. We take turns.
choices.feedback: Yes! Shared things aren't ours to trade. Everyone gets a fair turn.
Turns are shared fairly. They're not for trading.
The class iPad isn't yours to trade. Take turns.

items.text: A game asks you to buy more coins.

choices.feedback: Buying costs real money. Stop and ask a grown-up.
Yes! Always ask a grown-up before buying anything.

choices.text: Ask my friend to buy it
choices.feedback: Buying costs real money. Stop and ask a grown-up.

items.text: Your friend says: Let's take silly photos of everyone with the class iPad!

choices.feedback: Always ask people before taking their picture, and ask the teacher first.

choices.text: Say: Let's ask the teacher first
choices.feedback: Yes! The camera is for school work when the teacher says.
Even one photo needs permission. Ask the teacher first.

items.text: Oops! You drop your iPad and the screen cracks.

choices.text: Hide it so no one sees
choices.feedback: Hiding it makes it worse. Telling the truth is the brave choice.
Yes! Accidents happen. Telling right away is responsible.

choices.text: Put it back and say nothing
choices.feedback: The next friend might get hurt by the crack. Tell the teacher.

items.text: Your iPad battery is almost empty.

choices.text: Tell the teacher it needs charging
choices.feedback: Yes! Then it will be ready next time.

choices.text: Keep using it until it turns off
choices.feedback: Then your work might not save. Tell the teacher.

choices.text: Turn it off and put it away
choices.feedback: It still needs charging. Tell the teacher so it gets plugged in.

items.text: Your iPad time is over.

choices.text: Close my apps and put it back carefully
choices.feedback: Yes! Now it is ready for the next friend.
Someone else needs it next. Put it back where it belongs.

choices.text: Leave it on for the next friend
choices.feedback: Close the apps and put it back carefully.

activities.title: Ready for the Next Friend

activities.winSay: The iPad is charging and ready for the next friend! Sharing well keeps our class running.

activities.title: Where Do iPads Come From?
activities.intro: Let's find out how our iPads got to our classroom!
activities.winSay: Now you know where our iPads come from, and why we take care of them!

do.ask: How did the iPad get to our classroom? Tap the steps in order.

steps.label: Our school pays money for them

do.done: From the factory to our classroom!

do.ask: A producer makes things. A consumer buys and uses things. The company that makes iPads is a...

items.label: Producer
items.say: Yes! The company produces, or makes, the iPads.

items.label: Consumer

items.label: Consumer
items.say: Yes! Our school buys and uses iPads, so it is a consumer.

do.ask: A good is a thing you can touch. A service is work someone does for you. Tap the right box.

items.label: An iPad

items.label: Headphones
items.say: Headphones are a thing you can touch. Try again.

items.label: A charging cable
items.say: A cable is a thing you can touch. Try again.

items.label: Fixing a cracked screen
items.say: Fixing is work someone does for you. It is a service. Try again.

items.label: A teacher helping you log in
items.say: Helping is a service. Try again.

items.label: Internet from the Wi-Fi company
items.say: The internet company does work for us. It is a service. Try again.

do.done: You know goods and services!

do.ask: Fixing a cracked screen costs a lot of money. What does that mean for our class?

items.label: That money can't buy other things, like new books
items.say: Yes! Money spent on repairs can't be spent on other things we want.

items.label: Nothing. Fixing is free.
items.say: Fixing costs money. Try again.

items.label: The iPad fixes itself
items.say: iPads can't fix themselves! Try again.

do.done: Taking care of our iPads saves money for other things.

weeks.title: Screen Time, Green Time
weeks.bigIdea: Time is like money: we only have so much to spend each day. Screens can be fun, but our bodies and brains need a balance of screen time and green time.

words.meaning: time spent using a device like an iPad, TV or phone
time spent away from screens, like playing outside or reading a book
a good mix, so we don't do too much of one thing
a plan for how to spend your money, or your time

activities.title: Learn It: What Is Screen Time?
activities.intro: Let's learn about screen time! Listen carefully, then solve each puzzle to unlock Next.

slides.text: A screen is the glass you look at on an iPad, a TV or a phone.

do.ask: Which things have a screen? Find all four.

items.label: Paper book
items.say: A paper book has pages, not a screen. Keep looking.

items.label: Ball
items.say: A ball has no screen. Keep looking.

items.label: Crayons
items.say: Crayons have no screen. Keep looking.

do.done: You found all the screens!

slides.text: Screen time is the time we spend looking at screens.

do.ask: Which ones are screen time? Find all three.

items.label: Jump rope
items.say: Jumping rope is green time. Keep looking.

items.label: Read a comic book
items.say: A paper comic book is green time. Keep looking.

items.label: Build a blanket fort
items.say: Building a fort is green time. Keep looking.

do.done: Yes! Those all use a screen.

slides.text: Green time is time away from screens, like playing outside, reading or drawing.

do.ask: Screen time or green time? Tap the right box.

items.label: Ride a bike
items.say: Riding a bike is green time. Try again.

items.label: Watch a movie
items.say: A movie is on a screen. Try again.

items.label: Do a puzzle
items.say: A puzzle is green time. Try again.

items.label: Text a friend
items.say: Texting uses a screen. Try again.

items.label: Look at the stars
items.say: Stargazing is green time. Try again.

items.label: Read an e-book
items.say: An e-book is on a screen. Try again.

do.done: Great sorting!

slides.text: Screens can be fun and help us learn. But our eyes, bodies and brains need breaks.

do.ask: Which ones tell you your body needs a screen break? Find all three.

items.label: Feeling happy and rested
items.say: Happy and rested means your body feels good. Keep looking.

items.label: Excited to play outside
items.say: That's a great feeling! Keep looking.

do.done: Listen to your body. It tells you when to take a break.

slides.text: A healthy day has balance: some screen time and lots of green time.

do.ask: Which afternoon is balanced? Tap it.

items.label: Screens all afternoon
items.say: That's too much screen time. Try again.

items.label: Bike, book, one show, dinner
items.say: Yes! A little screen time and lots of green time.

items.label: Games until bedtime
items.say: That's too much screen time. Try again.

do.done: That's a balanced day!

slides.text: Time is like money. Each day you only have so much to spend, so spend it wisely!

do.ask: You have 3 hours to spend after school. Which plan spends your time wisely?

items.label: 1 hour play outside, 1 hour homework and reading, 1 hour show and dinner
items.say: Yes! You spent your time on lots of different things.

items.label: 3 hours of video games
items.say: You spent all your time on one thing. Try again.

items.label: 2 hours of videos, 1 hour of games
items.say: That spends all your time on screens. Try again.

do.done: Spend your time like money: on a good mix of things.

items.label: Me!
items.say: Yes! You are in charge of your time.

items.label: Nobody
items.say: Someone does decide. Try again.

do.done: You are the boss of your time!

choices.feedback: Yes! Your body needs green time.

weeks.title: Private and Personal
weeks.bigIdea: Some information is private. We keep it safe and only share it with grown-ups we trust.

words.meaning: facts about you that strangers should not know, like your address or password
a secret word that keeps your account safe
a grown-up who keeps you safe, like a parent or teacher
